title: Painkiller
description: Dark rum, pineapple, orange and coconut cream, shaken.
origin: Soggy Dollar Bar, British Virgin Islands, 1970s

steps.do: Combine everything in a shaker tin, fill with ice and shake hard. The shake whips air into the coconut cream.
Double strain (Hawthorne plus fine strainer) into the glass to keep the foam, then add fresh ice, cubed or crushed.
Grate nutmeg over the top and add a pineapple wedge.

items: Essentially a Piña Colada with orange juice and nutmeg added.
Homemade sweetened coconut cream keeps about 1 week, refrigerated. It separates and thickens when cold: shake or stir, and let it loosen at room temperature before measuring.
Unsweetened canned coconut milk: warm 1/2 cup full-fat coconut milk with 1/2 cup sugar, stirring just until dissolved, then cool. Use 1 oz in place of the sweetened coconut cream.
One drink, no batch: shake 1 oz full-fat coconut milk with 1/2 oz 2:1 simple syrup in place of the sweetened coconut cream.
Carton coconut milk (the thin drinking kind) won't work well. It makes a watery drink with little foam.

source.name: Strong, Sweet and Bitter: Your Guide to All Things Cocktails, Bartending and Booze from Behind the Bar by Cara Devine, p. 171
